all_of: a caching reverse proxy caches responses by URI plus a static extension and the backend treats the dot as a format delimiter
a response reaches a browser without a charset declaration
a page renders attacker-controlled markdown that becomes HTML attributes
a bot with a more privileged role visits an attacker-supplied URL
any_of: a Django view calls filter(**request.data) with a foreign key to the user model
a Rails controller merges params.to_unsafe_h after Marshal.dump into a JSON body

chain.action: confirm the proxy caches static-looking extensions: request an authenticated page as /path.html?cb=N twice and read X-Cache-Status MISS then HIT, then read it anonymously
chain.why: the cache key is the URI plus the extension, so an authenticated page can be stored under a static-looking URL

chain.action: store a markdown bio that uses the JIS X 0208 1978 escape to break out of an attribute and set onerror
chain.why: no charset is declared, so Chrome sniffs the encoding and the escaped quote is misread

chain.action: cache the authenticated settings page and report its internal http://127.0.0.1:<port>/settings.html?cb=N URL to the bot
chain.why: the bot is authenticated, and the cached page runs the XSS in its session; .html renders while .ico is treated as an image

chain.action: from the XSS, brute-force the admin password with GET /contracts/manage?owner__password__startswith=<prefix>&owner__username=admin
chain.why: Django filter(**request.data) follows the owner foreign key, so a matching prefix returns rows and the page stops saying 'No contracts found'

chain.action: have the XSS write the recovered password into the bot's own bio and navigate to a cacheable settings URL, then read it anonymously
chain.why: the cookie is HttpOnly, so the payload acts inside the page instead of stealing the session

chain.action: as admin, create a contract template whose data field overrides Marshal.dump via the params merge, using a Ruby 3.4 Gem::RequestSet::Lockfile gadget that runs a shell command through zip
chain.why: Marshal.load deserialises the stored data on view; the detection gadget must run first to create the git cache directory

chain.action: run cp /flag.txt into the Rails public directory and fetch it over HTTP
chain.why: the flag lives at the container root and the RCE runs in the Rails container

first_confirming_probe.request: authenticated GET /settings.html?cb=1 twice, then anonymous GET /settings.html?cb=1
first_confirming_probe.expected: the anonymous request returns 200 with X-Cache-Status HIT and the body of the authenticated page
first_confirming_probe.falsifier: the anonymous request is a 302 to /login, so the proxy does not serve an authenticated page anonymously

blast_radius: cache poisoning affects every player who requests the cached URL until it expires; the XSS and RCE act as the privileged bot and can write files inside the container, so use a disposable cachebuster and remove created templates

verification.evidence: the flag was written to the Rails public directory by the Marshal RCE and read back over HTTP 200 on the live target

reuse_when: an nginx location caches by extension and a Rails-style backend treats the dot as a format delimiter
a page renders markdown without a charset declaration
a Django endpoint calls filter(**request.data) with a foreign key to users
known_traps: report the internal 127.0.0.1 URL to the bot, not the public address, or the bot session is not used
.ico is rendered as an image by Chrome, so the cached HTML never executes; use .html
the Marshal gadget needs the detection step first or it raises Errno::ENOENT on the git cache directory
the gadget is tied to the exact Ruby and gem build and can fail on a patched image
the flag file written into the web root may not be removable afterwards; reset the instance
